# Skilled Worker visa: caseworker guidance

Immigration staff guidance on considering applications under the Skilled Worker route.

## Updates to this page

From:
    UK Visas and Immigration
Published:
    1 December 2020
Last updated:
    3 August 2026

  1. 3 August 2026

Updated to add information about Part Suitability update to immigration bail.

  2. 11 May 2026

Updated to add information about: correction to the settlement qualifying period information, clarification of transitional rules relating to the 4 April 2024 Rules changes, and clarification of CTA policy regarding switching.

  3. 8 April 2026

This guidance has been updated to add information about the prison officer allowance; the English language requirement for settlement; and the introduction of the visa brake for nationals of Afghanistan.

  4. 16 December 2025

Updated the table of charging costs for CoS assigned from 16 December 2025 in the accessible version to match the PDF.

  5. 16 December 2025

Updated with information about the English language requirements change from 8 January 2026 and the Immigration Skills Charge uplift.

  6. 11 November 2025

Updated to reflect the addition of Part Suitability to the Immigration Rules.

  7. 22 July 2025

The guidance has been updated to reflect the Immigration Rules change on 22 July 2025.

  8. 9 April 2025

Updated the guidance to reflect Immigration Rules changes.

  9. 27 November 2024

Updated to reflect the change to e-Visas.

  10. 8 October 2024

The guidance has been updated to make minor clarifications and corrections, in particular to switching, appropriate SOC codes, London weighting, supplementary employment, and salary requirements at settlement. Some of these updates reflect Immigration Rules changes on 8 October 2024.

  11. 4 April 2024

Updated the minimum salary thresholds for the Skilled Worker visa. A full list of changes is in the 'Changes from last version of this guidance' section.

  12. 11 March 2024

The guidance has been updated narrow the eligibility for care workers and senior care workers in England to be sponsored only where the sponsor is registered with the Care Quality Commission and is currently carrying on a regulated activity, with transitional arrangements for workers already in the route.
